MorphoHand · real_v1 / SR2 hand, D8 gantry · controller of arXiv 2609.25619 · 1–2 October 2026 · built 2026-10-02 11:12

Relative contact-velocity control of the screwdriver pick, braked swing and peg-hole insertion on the SR2 hand in MuJoCo and Drake

On the nominal trial the chain completes in the three contact models that carry pinch friction torque. D8 picks the screwdriver off two posts with a thumb–index pinch, lifts it, brakes its gravity swing to hanging, squeezes it to 3 N and pushes it 22–22 mm into a 1 mm-clearance peg hole. A closed-loop brake that sets the pinch force every 10 ms ends the swing at 92.4° in Drake hydroelastic, 90.5° with MuJoCo 1 mm sphere fingertips and 88.2° with MuJoCo condim 4. The paper’s open-loop force reduction stops at 79.1°. Point contact fails in both simulators: with no pinch torque the tool swings free as soon as it is lifted. Across ten perturbed seeds the pick fails in 8 of 10, so the brake’s reliability is not yet measured. Per simulated second, MuJoCo condim 4 costs 40 ms of one core, 1 mm sphere fingertips 104 ms and Drake hydroelastic 2212 ms.

Controller and chain

the paper’s generalized contact frames and least squares, a pad force through the servos, a closed-loop brake

Each fingertip gets a generalized contact frame on the tool: origin at the witness points, x along the tool’s signed-distance gradient, y the finger’s flexion axis projected on the tangent plane. The relative contact twist (spin, two roll, separation, two slide components; paper Eq. 1) is linear in the finger’s three joint rates. The joint-rate reference is the bounded least squares of Eq. 2, with damping and healthy-pose terms, integrated into the servo targets at 100 Hz. For a sphere against a cylinder the frames are exact in closed form and stay smooth through contact, so the paper’s geodesic filter on the hydroelastic centre of pressure is left out. The controller runs on a kinematic MuJoCo copy of the scene, so the same code drives the MuJoCo and the Drake plant.

The chain has seven steps.

  • Pick: the palm descends with thumb and index 8 mm open. They close along their contact normals (vsep = −15 mm/s, slide held at zero) and switch to force at contact. Pad force F enters as q = qtouch + JT(−F n)/kp + τg/kp, with τg the fingers’ own weight.
  • Lift: the palm rises 90 mm at F = 4 N.
  • Brake: the swing about the pinch axis runs open loop (4 → 0.5 N over 3 s) or closed loop. The closed-loop brake tracks a 1.8 s minimum-jerk profile to 90°. It inverts Iφ̈ = mgd cosφ − τf(N) through the rig’s brake law, with nominal mass and μ. Its force floor starts at twice the slip limit W/2μ, falls while the tool stalls off vertical, and rises 50 % when the tool slides along its axis. It accepts the swing within 2.5°.
  • Hold firm: F rises to 3 N.
  • Transport and aim: the palm carries the tool’s lower end, aimed from its measured pose, 8 mm over the hole and corrects once.
  • Insert: the palm descends 30 mm at 15 mm/s.

The pinch line is the thumb–index mount line turned 45° about the palm normal, 50 mm below the mounts. There both fingers keep 0.55 rad of joint range from 4 mm squeeze to 12 mm open. The 2026-10-01 brake study’s line through the mount midpoint at 45 mm puts the index on its mcp and pip limits at contact, and the pinch cannot open there.

Swing ends = angle about the pinch axis when the brake phase ends (90° = hanging). After squeeze = the same angle once the pad force is at the hold value. Inserted = depth of the lower end below the block top when the palm stops (goal 20 mm, hole 30 mm deep). Lower end tilt = tool axis from vertical, in and out of the swing plane. Axial slip = travel of the tool along its axis through the pinch from the brake onward. Chain = pick, swing within 5°, hold within 5°, and inserted 15 mm or more on two pads.

Ten perturbed trials

tool ±3 mm and ±5° on the posts, μ 0.7–1.3, mass ±20 %, perception noise 0.5 mm and 1°

model brake pick swing within 5° hold within 5° inserted chain swing end, completed
MuJoCo condim 4, μt rescheduled open loop 2/10 1/10 1/10 2/10 1/10 85.0°
MuJoCo condim 4, μt rescheduled closed loop 2/10 1/10 1/10 1/10 1/10 89.5°
MuJoCo 1 mm sphere fingertips (205 per pad) open loop 2/10 1/10 1/10 2/10 1/10 87.2°
MuJoCo 1 mm sphere fingertips (205 per pad) closed loop 2/10 1/10 1/10 1/10 1/10 90.3°

The pick is the first step that breaks. In 5 seeds one finger stalls short of contact within the 2.5 s close window. In 3 more the pinch closes late and the tool falls out during the lift. The same seeds fail in both contact models and under both brakes, before the brake runs. Seeds 3, 9 pick cleanly. On seed 3 (μ 1.05, mass ×0.84) the closed-loop brake completes the chain in both MuJoCo models (89.5° and 90.3°), and the open-loop brake ends the swing at 81.6° and 84.4° (chain failed in condim 4, failed with spheres). On seed 9 (μ 1.17, mass ×1.09) the closed-loop brake drops the tool during the swing in both, and the open-loop brake completes the chain in both MuJoCo models (85.0° and 87.2°).

Experiment 1: contact-free tracking

the index steps each relative-velocity component at 40 °/s or 20 mm/s while the other five are held at zero

servo sep gain slide y gain slide z gain spin gain roll y gain roll z gain RMSE angular RMSE linear closest approach
calibrated, kp 0.5 0.86 0.92 0.66 0.35 0.14 0.03 24.3 °/s 7.0 mm/s 6.5 mm
template, kp 30 0.88 0.93 0.65 0.35 0.14 0.03 23.7 °/s 5.5 mm/s 6.5 mm

Gain = median achieved/commanded on the stepped component while it is stepped. RMSE over the whole 7.8 s sequence, all three angular or all three linear components. Closest approach = smallest tip-to-cylinder distance; contact-free when positive. 500 Hz control as in the paper.

With all six components weighted equally, as in the paper’s protocol, a three-joint finger cannot follow a pure step. It translates its tip only by turning it, so the least squares trades each commanded component against the five held at zero. The gain is the median ratio of achieved to commanded on the stepped component. The mean gain on the linear steps is 0.81 on the calibrated servo and 0.82 on the template servo; on the angular steps 0.17 and 0.18. The two servos agree, so the shortfall is the finger's kinematics, not servo lag. The paper reports RMSE for five hands in a figure without stating the values in its text.

The cost is the wall time of the nominal chain with the closed-loop brake and no film, on one core of the workstation. It covers 10–13 s of simulation at a 1 ms step plus the 100 Hz controller, IK setup included. The 0.5 mm sphere pad (819 spheres) is not timed: its per-sphere spring cannot reach a 0.02 s relaxation inside MuJoCo’s soft-contact range. The rig page reports its torque accuracy at a 0.02 s relaxation on the two-pad rig.

What this does not settle

  1. The pick under perturbation. Eight of ten perturbed picks fail before the brake. The next step is a per-seed trace of the close phase in hom_chain.run_chain: tip-to-surface distance, joint margins and tool displacement on the posts. Candidate fixes are position feedback on the slide references (the closing tilts the pinch line 1.3°) and a V-cradle instead of flat posts. Re-run seeds 1–10. The brake comparison counts only once the pick holds on at least 9 of 10 seeds.
  2. The closed-loop brake’s drop on seed 9. With a 9 % heavier tool and μ 1.17 the closed-loop brake lost the tool mid-swing in both MuJoCo models, where the open-loop schedule completed the chain. The brake inverts the law with the nominal mass, and its force floor of 2 W/2μ is set from it. That trace (hom_chain.py run --spec mj:point4s --seed 9) is the first to read: floor, commanded force and axial slip against time.
  3. Brake reliability. With picks fixed, run 20 seeds per brake in condim 4 and the sphere model, and 10 in Drake hydroelastic (about 5 min). Report the final-angle spread and drops. The open-loop schedule should be tuned on the nominal trial first, since the paper’s operator ended the force reduction by eye.
  4. Out-of-plane tilt. In MuJoCo the hanging tool leans 1.5–2.3° out of the swing plane, following the pinch line’s tilt; in Drake about 1°. A hold-phase correction moving the two tips about 0.8 mm vertically in opposite directions is written up in the session notes but not run.
  5. The three-pad hold. “Hold firm again” is a two-pad squeeze here. D8’s deploy-plan grasp, where the middle releases and re-closes on the hanging shaft (the 2026-09-16 swing), is the follow-up chain.
  6. The bench. The closed-loop brake reads the swing angle at 100 Hz from the tool pose. The AprilTag tracker’s rate and latency, and the pad modulus behind E = 10 MPa, are unmeasured.
